intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome (ABERS) is caused by mutation in the TBX22 gene (300307) on chromosome Xq21.1.

paragraphs.text: Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome is characterized by cleft palate, coloboma, hypospadias, deafness, short stature, and radial synostosis (Abruzzo and Erickson, 1977). The disorder has been described as X-linked and CHARGE-like, and it has been shown to be allelic to classic X-linked cleft palate (Pauws et al., 2013).

checks.explanation: The abstract lists exactly these six features.

checks.evidence_quote: confirms that TBX22 is the gene underlying Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome, expanding the phenotypic spectrum of TBX22 mutations
checks.explanation: Both CPX and ABERS are caused by TBX22 mutations, so the two are allelic.

paragraphs.text: Metlay et al. (1987) reported a boy with CHARGE syndrome who had a coloboma of the optic nerve head, congenital heart defects (ASD, VSD, and parachute mitral valve), choanal atresia, severe growth retardation, genital hypoplasia, abnormal ears, cleft lip and palate, and pectus carinatum. His chromosomes were normal, and he died at 19 months. His mother was short and had hearing impairment, choanal atresia, and a coloboma.

paragraphs.text: Abruzzo and Erickson (1989) did a follow-up study of the family they had reported earlier with cleft palate, coloboma, hypospadias, deafness, short stature, and radial synostosis. This family had been cited as an example of familial CHARGE syndrome, but the authors concluded that the patients did not have familial CHARGE syndrome.

paragraphs.text: The finding by Pauws et al. (2013) of a mutation in the X-linked TBX22 gene that tracked with the phenotype in the Abruzzo-Erickson family supported X-linked inheritance.

checks.claim: Pauws et al. (2013) found a mutation in the X-linked TBX22 gene that tracked with the phenotype in the Abruzzo-Erickson family.
checks.evidence_quote: A novel TBX22 splice acceptor mutation (c.593-5T>A) was identified that tracked with the phenotype in this family.

checks.claim: The TBX22 mutation tracking with the phenotype in the Abruzzo-Erickson family supported X-linked inheritance of Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: A novel TBX22 splice acceptor mutation (c.593-5T>A) was identified that tracked with the phenotype in this family.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the family as X-linked and reports cosegregation, but it does not explicitly say this supports X-linked inheritance. That is an inference.

paragraphs.text: Pauws et al. (2013) hypothesized that TBX22 might be involved in the family with X-linked, CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome originally reported by Abruzzo and Erickson (1977). They identified a novel TBX22 splice acceptor mutation (c.593-5T-A) that tracked with the phenotype in the family. In patients with classic X-linked cleft palate phenotypes, they also found a novel TBX22 splice donor variant (c.767+5G-A) and a known canonical splice donor mutation (c.767+1G-A), both affecting the same exon as the Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome mutation. In silico and in vitro splicing studies predicted that all 3 variants abolished normal mRNA splicing, and an in vitro assay indicated that use of alternative splice sites was a likely outcome. Pauws et al. (2013) concluded that TBX22 is the gene underlying Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome, which expands the phenotypic spectrum of TBX22 mutations.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of the family with X-linked, CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome, who had sensorineural deafness and coloboma, Pauws et al. (2013) identified a novel splice acceptor mutation (c.593-5T-A) in the TBX22 gene. The mutation tracked with the phenotype in the family. In silico and in vitro splicing studies predicted that the mutation abolished normal mRNA splicing, and an in vitro assay indicated that use of alternative splice sites was a likely outcome.
